items.title: Hackers Hide Malware Infrastructure on Polygon Blockchain and Trick Users Into Running It With ClickFix
items.description: Hackers are using the Polygon blockchain to keep parts of a malware operation out of plain sight. The campaign, tracked as ErrTraffic, turns hacked WordPress sites into launch points for fake verification prompts that persuade visitors to run harmful Windows commands. items.title: A Malicious SIM Card Can Run Attacker Code Inside the Modems Behind Cellular IoT Devices
items.description: A malicious SIM card can order the device it sits in to run commands of the attacker's choosing. On the cellular modules built into electric-vehicle chargers, industrial routers, and car telematics units, that is enough to take the whole device over. items.description: Mozilla has scrapped the cryptographic key behind Firefox and Thunderbird downloads for Linux after an unencrypted copy of it was committed by mistake to one of the company's own private code repositories. The campaign moved from a wind-farm network into a heat and power plant, turning trusted connectivity into disruption. items.description: Chinese-speaking cybercriminals are using fake software pages that imitate popular artificial intelligence tools to infect Windows users with remote access malware.
